hints.title: Cell Quadrant Sub-division
hints.text: Subdivide each one-by-one cell into four triangular regions: top, right, bottom, and left.

hints.title: Slash Connectivity Rules
hints.text: A forward slash connects top with left and right with bottom. A backslash connects top with right and bottom with left. A space connects all four quadrants.

hints.title: Boundary Sharing Disjoint Sets
hints.text: Number quadrants across the n by n grid as 4 * (r * n + c) + k for k in [0, 1, 2, 3]. Connect internal quadrants per character, and connect each cell bottom quadrant to the cell below top quadrant, and right quadrant to neighbor left quadrant. Count distinct root components.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph flood fill on fractional boundaries is cumbersome without sub-pixel grid dilation or quadrant decomposition.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Splitting each cell into 4 quadrants produces exactly 4 * N^2 disjoint set elements with near-constant union-find operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that 4 triangles per grid cell cleanly represent planar connectivity without floating point math.
complexity.notes: An alternative is 3x3 pixel dilation with standard BFS flood fill, but 4-quadrant DSU uses less memory.
